- **Given back** when what they paid for couldn't be made (`inf_refund`, once; a month's free ones only that month).
  **No cash value:** never withdrawn, sold or refunded (the page says so).
- **Prices** (`PRICES` in `src/studio/rules.js`, the owner's choice; Crush 20% off, Soulmate 40% off: `DISCOUNT`):

  | What | Stranger | Crush | Soulmate |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | A new influencer (its 4 looks and its full body) | 100 | 80 | 60 |
  | 4 new looks | 40 | 32 | 24 |
  | A photo | 15 | 12 | 9 |
  | A trend video | 300 | 240 | 180 |
  | A 5-second video | 400 | 320 | 240 |
  | A 3D model | 500 | 400 | 300 (the first each month free) |

**Its 3D models** are the 3D studio's characters (`supabase/studio.sql`), now made from the influencer's full-body picture
(Meshy's image to 3D, then its bones and 8 moves: 59 of Meshy's credits), paid in credits (`inf_3d`, one at a time per
influencer), inside the studio's characters a month (`STUDIO_A_MONTH`); one that can't be made gives its credits back (or
a Soulmate's free one). Since round 2 also for a big burn instead (`STUDIO_MODEL_BURN_AGI`, 25,000 $AGI: "AGI Studio,
round 2"). **Its coin** is a launch draft like her bot's (`coinDraft()`): her checks of the name, ticker and
line, its picture the picked look from our bucket (`studio:<influencer>/<job>-<n>`, a JPEG of 1 MB at most), and a
scrambled code of the wallet instead of a Telegram chat; from there, the launch page's own rules (hard rule 9's exception).
While `LAUNCH_ONLY_FOR` is set, only the owner and `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`'s wallets get a link.

**Limits:** 3 influencers being made at once per wallet (since round 2 also `STUDIO_SLOTS`, 5, in all, and one more for
each slot unlocked by burning), 4 photos and videos at once, 30 uploads a day, 50 likes a day (round 2), 2,000 AI jobs a
day for the whole site (`STUDIO_JOBS_A_DAY`: each paid in credits, a guard against a runaway), 10 reports a day each; speed
bumps per server copy (60 looks, 20 actions, 90 upload parts and 300 files a minute per visitor).

**Deleting** (`inf_delete`): gone from every page at once, what's being made for it stopped (its credits back), its 3D
models taken down, its files deleted (the tidy-up deletes anything left). **Reports:** anyone (the human check, 7 reasons:
a real person who didn't agree, looks like a minor, sexual, hate, violence, someone else's character, something else),
under a daily code of who reported; the owner's page lists them, takes things down (`inf_hide`, `inf_job_hide`) or clears
them. **The tidy-up** (every 30 minutes, with the clock): uploads after 2 days (a selfie or a picture as soon as its
influencer is made), influencers that couldn't be made after 30 days, deleted ones after a week, failed jobs after 60
days, reports after 90.

**Its files:** the 3D studio's private bucket (`agi1-characters`, since then JPEG pictures and a clip's parts too):
`inf/<influencer>/…` (pictures, videos, posters; since round 2 a video's copy with the share mark, `<job>.dl.mp4`),
`trends/…`, `examples/…` (round 2) and `up/…` (uploads). Served from our own address in a sandbox (`?inf-file=`;
`?inf-video=` in parts like the studio's videos; `?inf-video-dl=` a signed address, 2 hours; since round 2 `?inf-dl=` a
photo with the share mark and `?inf-ex=` an example picture); a private one's are never kept by the CDN, so deleting it
("Delete my face" for an AI twin) takes them off at once.

**Its addresses** (`vercel.json`, `vite.config.js`): `/studio/:path+` serves the app's page; on the host studio.agi1.app
every address that isn't a file serves it (a rewrite), and "/" there goes to /explore (a redirect: Vercel serves
`index.html` at "/" before any rewrite). Everything it asks goes to `/api/launch` (`server/inf-api.js`: no 13th function).
The page's CSP got `media-src 'self' blob:` (its videos from our own address, and a visitor's own clip in their browser)
and `Permissions-Policy` `camera=(self)` (the live selfie), for our own pages only; since round 2 `camera=()` again (no
selfies: no page of the site may use the camera).

**What's kept** (`supabase/influencers.sql`, row level security on, only the server's key): per influencer a scrambled
code of its wallet (never the address), its name, how it was made, its style and choices, the upload it was made from
(only until it's made), which look was picked, and whether it's in Explore or hidden; each picture or video made for it
(its words, shape and sound, its credits, where it is at the AI service, its files' count and size); per wallet code its
credits, and a log of each top-up, spend, refund and free grant; per month the free credits given; each upload's kind and
whether it passed; the trend moves; reports (why, and a daily code of who reported); per day the AI jobs started; since
round 2 whether an upload and its influencer are a real person's photo, likes (per creation, a scrambled code of the wallet
that liked it and its level), each week's spotlight (and once its prize is claimed, the address it went to and its
transaction: 60 days), burn unlocks and the extra influencers a wallet unlocked; since round 4 a wallet's clank.trade name
(if it shows one), its AI captions and helper answers a day, support tickets and bans (see "AGI Studio, round 4"), and since
its phase 3 each gift (scrambled codes of both wallets and how the page shows them, its credits, its note, a gift link's
secret: until a year after it's done) and who joined through whose invite, with its rewards. Never an address (but a
prize's), a transaction (but a prize's), an IP address or anything else about anyone. The safety note's 01, 02, 03 and 04
say so.

**The old 3D studio's orders** (`api/launch.js`): a character from words (`studio-quote`) and a character's video
(`studio-video-quote`) answer **410 `moved`**; a character's page, its files and its videos still answer, and so does
finishing an order made before (choosing how to pay, "Check my payment", making one again).

**Setup (the owner, in this order):**
1. **Vercel Pro** (selling credits is commercial use: Hobby doesn't allow it): Vercel → the team's Settings → Billing.
2. **fal.ai** (if not done for the studio's videos): fal.ai → sign up → **Billing**: a balance (each picture and video is
   taken from it; when it's empty, things wait) → **API Keys** → a new key → Vercel → `FAL_KEY` (Production). A secret:
   never in chat, code, git or a screenshot.
3. **Supabase** → SQL Editor: **all** of `supabase/studio.sql` again (after `burns.sql`; it keeps everything and ends with
   `studio_ready = 1`), then **all** of `supabase/influencers.sql` (it ends with `influencers_ready = 1`; since round 2 its
   version of round 2: run it again if it was run before, before pushing round 2).
4. **Vercel** → Environment Variables (Production): `STUDIO_PAY_TO` (the owner's own wallet address on Robinhood Chain:
   where USDG for credits goes; an address, never a key), `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR` (the owner's wallet: private first; its first
   wallet is the owner's page's, unless `STUDIO_OWNER` names another). Optional: `STUDIO_FACES` = `off` (since round 2:
   no photos of real people, only drawings and characters; before: no AI twins), `STUDIO_FREE_CREDITS_A_MONTH` (5000),
   `STUDIO_JOBS_A_DAY` (2000), `MESHY_API_KEY` (3D models: the studio's setup), `PINATA_JWT` (coins: Launch with AGI-1's);
   since round 2 `PRIZE_WALLET_KEY` (her quizzes' prize wallet: the weekly spotlight's prize comes from it; without it
   the spotlight is for glory only), `STUDIO_WEEKLY_PRIZE` (10000), `STUDIO_SLOTS` (5), `STUDIO_SLOT_AGI` (5000),
   `STUDIO_BOOST_AGI` (10000), `STUDIO_MODEL_BURN_AGI` (25000), `STUDIO_BURNS_A_MONTH` (10). Then **Redeploy**.
5. **The domain:** Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Settings → **Domains** → **Add Domain** → `studio.agi1.app` → the DNS record it
   shows (a CNAME) → Namecheap's hosting **cPanel → Zone Editor** (like inference.agi1.app: see "CloakMesh at
   inference.agi1.app") → wait for "Valid Configuration". Until then the app is at agi1.app/studio. Cloudflare's human
   check needs nothing (agi1.app's widget covers its subdomains).
6. **Push.**
7. **The trend clips and example pictures** (since round 2; trend moves before, about $0.84 each): at
   studio.agi1.app/owner (or agi1.app/studio/owner) with the owner's wallet: **Make the 12 missing clips** (about $1.26
   each from fal's balance, about $15 in all, a few minutes each), watch each, **Keep** the good ones (**Make it again** for
   one that isn't); then **Make the 32 missing pictures** (about $0.08 each, about $2.60), and **Again** for one that
   isn't right. Until a clip is kept, the trend sheet says "No trending clips yet: use your own clip."; until a picture is
   made, its choice shows only its words.
8. **Try it** with the owner's wallet: buy a few credits ($5), design one, pick a look, a photo, a trend video, a video, a
   3D model, a coin link (open it only to look: launching makes a real coin); then (round 2) "From a photo" with a photo of
   yourself (it's private: never in Explore), a like, a download (its mark), and Delete.
9. **Before opening it** (`STUDIO_OPEN` = `yes`): the AI services' terms for selling what they make (see "Open
   questions"), then a link to it from the other pages (Claude adds it).

### AGI Studio, round 2 (2026-10-10)

**The owner's list** (after looking at AGI Studio the same day): "remove the use your face"; "no restrictions on That
looks like a photo of a real person" (the owner's pick: **"Allowed with consent (Recommended)"**); "the trending videos
should be real like in higgsfield genjutsu" (the owner: "from higgsfield trending with promps with them, just look up
higgsfield"); "in the make it yours show example of the image not just text"; "the site looks mid lol unlike higgsfield,
make the design like higs field just change it a bit so it doesn't look alike"; "large burns can make free 3d model" (the
owner's pick: **25,000 $AGI**); and Claude's flywheel, all four parts the owner picked: **a share mark**, **a weekly
spotlight with a prize**, **burn unlocks** and **a live stats board** (with likes, which the spotlight needs). Built the
same day, in the same app (no new function file, no new service, no new secret). **Run `supabase/influencers.sql` again
before pushing it** (it keeps everything saved; it ends with `influencers_ready = 1`).

**Photos of real people, with consent; no "Use my face":**
- No live camera anywhere (`Permissions-Policy` `camera=()` again; no `getUserMedia` in the app: a test fails the build
  otherwise). Create's two ways are **Design it** and **From a photo**: a photo of you, of a friend who said OK, or a
  character you drew or rendered, picked only once the box is ticked ("This is me, someone who said I may use their photo
  (an adult), or a character of my own."), which our server needs too (`consent`, else 400).
- Gemini looks at it before it's kept (`checkPicture()`): one person or character, clearly looking 21 or older (for a
  photo, its guessed age too); **never a famous person** (a celebrity, a public figure, a big influencer, photographed or drawn), a
  well-known character or mascot, anything sexual, hateful or violent. A photo is marked `real`. **Since 2026-10-11 fewer
  false alarms** (the owner: "can you make this no restrictions", then "any picture can upload"): famous only when the AI
  recognizes one specific, widely known person and is at least 70% sure (`FAMOUS_SURE`; unsure how sure: refused), so
  lookalikes and styled photos of people it doesn't recognize pass; a character only when it recognizes a specific well-known
  one (an original anime-style character passes); only the picture's subjects counted as people (not small or blurred people
  in the background); violent only gore, blood, graphic violence or a weapon used to threaten (a costume or fantasy prop held
  in a family-friendly way passes); "other" only a child anywhere, drug use, self-harm or shocking content.
- An influencer made from a real person's photo is **private**, like an AI twin was: never in Explore, never liked,
  spotlit or boosted, its files never kept by the CDN, its full body made with the photo too; deleting it deletes the
  photo and everything made from it. Its coin needs a second box (a real person's face on a public coin, for good).
- `STUDIO_FACES` = `off` now means only drawings and characters (Create says "photos of real people are switched off for
  now", said again when the studio's settings arrive after the page is drawn: a bug the browser test found and fixed).
- Influencers made from a face before round 2 stay as they were (private, "Delete my face"); no new ones.

**Real-looking trend videos:**
- The owner's **12 trend clips** (`TRENDS` in `src/studio/rules.js`): Golden hour, Paparazzi, Rooftop orbit, Neon crash
  zoom, Confetti freeze, Neon runway, Night drive, Rain twirl, Sunset run, Front row, First snow, Fireworks: each a short
  cinematic scene with a made-up young adult, its own camera move and its own sound, made once from words by Kling V3
  Standard's text to video (10 s, 9:16, with sound: about $1.26 each, about $15 for all 12) on the owner's page and kept by
  the owner. Like the trending templates people make with AI video apps; ours, written for this app: never anyone's video,
  music or name.
- **A trend video** puts the influencer into one (Kling O1 Edit, video to video: its picked look as its face, its full
  body and the photo it starts from as more views of it) in place of the clip's person, keeping the clip's moves, camera,
  place, light and sound (`keep_audio`), about $0.126 a second. Or into **their own clip** (3 to 10 s, 720 to 2160 px a
  side, 24 to 60 frames a second: the model's own limits, read from the clip's own header by `server/mp4.js`; its sound
  never used, since it could be someone else's music or voice). Still 300 credits.

**Example pictures** ("make it yours"): each of Create's choices with a picture: its 3 styles, 3 looks, 4 ages, 8 hair
styles, 8 outfits and 6 vibes, **32 pictures**, each one made-up adult showing only that choice (Nano Banana 2, 1:1, about
$0.08 each: about $2.60 for all), made once by the owner on the owner's page (**Make the 32 missing pictures**, **Again**
for one). Skin, hair color and eyes are color swatches instead. Served at `?inf-ex=<job>.webp` (kept a day by the CDN);
a choice without its picture shows its words.

**A new look** (`src/styles/studio-app.css`): media first, near-black, big pictures and videos in walls and rails,
condensed heavy headings (Anybody, the site's own font, its width narrowed), one violet-to-pink gradient for what to
press, honey for credits. Higgsfield's spirit, never its colors, logo, pictures or code. Still every rule an `sa-` class.

**The flywheel:**
- **Likes:** a heart on every done photo and video of a public influencer (never a private one, never your own), for any
  signed-in wallet, 50 a day (`inf_like`). Everyone's likes show; **only holders' (Crush and Soulmate, by their level when
  they liked) count toward the spotlight**, so a pile of new wallets can't pick it.
- **The weekly spotlight** (`server/inf-week.js`): each Monday (UTC) the studio's clock picks the week before once
  (`inf_week_pick`): its photo or video with the most holders' likes (at least one), then all likes, then the first made,
  of a public influencer. It waits on the owner's page: **Approve** (with its prize in whole $AGI, `STUDIO_WEEKLY_PRIZE`,
  10,000 by default, 0 = for glory) or **Skip to the next best**. Approved, it's Explore's "Spotlight of the week" for two
  weeks, and its maker sees it in My studio and claims the prize there: to the wallet they're signed in with (the one that
  made it), claimed in the database first (once), then $AGI's own transfer from **her quizzes' prize wallet**
  (`PRIZE_WALLET_KEY`), recorded before it goes out, never twice (`server/hot-wallet.js`); a claim left behind is given
  back after 2 minutes. Without the prize wallet, spotlights are for glory only. "A thank-you for making, not an
  investment, not financial advice": never paid to holders for holding.
- **Burn unlocks** (`server/inf-burns.js`): $AGI burned from the person's own wallet app (to `0x…dEaD`: never asked of a
  wallet, hard rule 9), read on Robinhood Chain like every burn, each burn counted once (in studio.sql's and burns.sql's
  ledgers: never also for messages or a character) and toward the wallet's level. A quote first (a day to burn toward it),
  then **Check my burn** (or a pasted link); burns add up:
  - **one more influencer** (`STUDIO_SLOT_AGI`, 5,000 $AGI): a wallet may have `STUDIO_SLOTS` (5) influencers being made
    or ready, and one more for each slot unlocked ("Unlock one more" in My studio; deleting one makes room);
  - **a boost** (`STUDIO_BOOST_AGI`, 10,000 $AGI): one of its own public influencers in Explore's **Boosted** row for 24
    hours (added to a boost already on);
  - **a free 3D model** (`STUDIO_MODEL_BURN_AGI`, 25,000 $AGI, the owner's): the 3D studio's own burn order (`inf_3d_burn`,
    checked by `checkPayment`), inside `STUDIO_BURNS_A_MONTH` (now 10 a month, was 5); one that can't be made is made again
    free (a burn can't be given back).
  "A burn is gone for good: not an investment, no refunds, not financial advice."
- **The share mark** (`server/inf-mark.js`): every photo and video downloaded carries a small "Made with AGI Studio ·
  AI-generated · studio.agi1.app" pill (`server/media/studio-mark.png`, drawn once by `tools/studio/mark.mjs`). A photo:
  marked with sharp as it's downloaded (`?inf-dl=<inf>/<job>-<n>.jpg`, bottom right). A video: marked once by the studio's
  clock (`/api/feed?studio`, one at a time, only with 14 s left, the newest first, 3 tries), top left (TikTok's, Reels' and
  Shorts' buttons sit at the bottom right), its picture encoded again, its sound copied as it is, kept beside it
  (`<job>.dl.mp4`); its downloads use that copy from then on, and the video as it plays on its page never changes. ffmpeg
  is the `@ffmpeg-installer/ffmpeg` package's Linux binary (ffmpeg 4.1, GPLv3, 66 MB), shipped with `/api/feed` only
  (`vercel.json`: `includeFiles`); it only ever reads videos the AI service made, never a visitor's upload.
- **The live stats board** at the top of Explore (`?inf-stats`, kept a minute): influencers, photos, videos, 3D models,
  made today, likes, $AGI burned in the studio and boosted now. Public totals only; hidden while everything is 0.

**Its addresses** (all in `/api/launch`): GET `?inf-dl=`, `?inf-ex=`, `?inf-stats`; POST `inf-like`, `inf-liked`,
`inf-3d-burn`, `inf-3d-check`, `inf-3d-redo`, `inf-burn-quote`, `inf-burn-check`, `inf-week-claim`, and the owner's
`inf-example-make`, `inf-week-set`; `?inf-info` adds `examples`, `burns`, `slots`, `weeklyPrize` and `likesADay`, and
`?inf-explore` adds `boosted` and `spotlight`.

**What's new in the database** (`supabase/influencers.sql`, 13 tables and 59 functions): `agi1_inf_likes` (per creation, a
scrambled code of the wallet that liked it and its level), `agi1_inf_weeks` (each week's spotlight; a claimed prize keeps
the address it went to and its transaction: the address 60 days after it's sent), `agi1_inf_burns` and `agi1_inf_slots`;
columns for a real person's photo (`real`), a boost (`boost_until`), example pictures (`example`), the share mark
(`marked`, `mark_tries`, `mark_at`) and likes. Row level security on all 13 tables, only the server's key.

### AGI Studio, round 4 (2026-10-11)

**The owner's list** (13 things after round 3; the owner picked each one's details one by one, then "im gonna sleep now":
nothing goes live without the owner, so Claude builds it in four phases, each tested and saved in this folder with its
steps): 1. a percentage and the time left while things are made, like Meshy's; 2. referrals (credits only); 3. gifting
bought credits; 4. a menu of video and image models (their references, seconds and quality; prices about 1.8× the AI's
cost; long videos up to 60 s); 5. tutorials; 6. clank.trade usernames; 7. support (an AI helper and tickets); 8. mod
commands; 9. an owner's tab (the AI services' balances, top-up links, low-balance alerts on Telegram); 10. X banners; 11.
memes with their photo and several references; 12. captions; 13. a one-click mode (its own name and color: the owner,
"call it a different name on that mode with differen color as well like fast , i dont know you know the best"). **Phase 1
(1, 10, 12, 6): built**, below. **Phase 2 (9, 8, 7): built**, after it: the owner's tab, Mod tools, Help & support. **Phase
3 (3, 2): built**, after phase 2: gifts of credits, gift links, invites. Phase 4: the model menu and long videos, memes, the
one-click mode; tutorials last.

**Progress bars** (the owner: "theres should be a percentage when they are creating the 3d model just like in meshy so
they know how long will it take"):
- Wherever something is being made (an influencer's looks and its full body, a photo, an X banner, a trend video, a video,
  a 3D model on its influencer's page and on its own page, the owner's trend clips): a bar, its percentage and the time
  left ("42% · about 3 min left", "under a minute left", and "taking longer than usual" past 1.6 times its usual time).
  Screen readers get a real progress bar ("Making its photo", "42%, about 3 min left").
- **Where it is comes from our server:** its step (in line, being made, being kept), when it started (our server's clock:
  the page lines its own up with it, so a device whose clock is off still shows the right numbers) and, for a 3D model,
  Meshy's own percentage of its step. How long each step usually takes is `TYPICAL` in `src/studio/rules.js`: an
  estimate, never a promise.
- **It moves every second by itself** (one timer for the whole app, resting while the tab is hidden) and **never goes
  back**. A step without a percentage of its own is as far along as the time since it started says, or as the time the
  page has seen it in that step says, whichever is further (round 4's browser check: a step that came sooner than usual sat
  still for seconds otherwise); at most 90% of a step until the next one comes, 99% at most, 5 s left at least.
- How: `src/studio/progress.js` (`progressBar()`, `barState()`, `tickBars()`, `noteServerNow()`) and `progressOf()` in
  `src/studio/rules.js`; our server's answers carry `now`, each job its `created`, and a 3D model being made its `progress`
  (its step and Meshy's percentage, read from Meshy at each look). Its width through a CSS variable (the CSP forbids style
  attributes).

**X banners** (the owner: "on the photos they can ghenerate the banner on their X as well with the right size"):
- The Photo tool's shapes are Vertical 9:16 · Wide 16:9 · Square 1:1 · **X banner 3:1** ("Exactly 1500 × 500, ready for
  your X header. Mira sits on the right: the lower left stays clear for your profile picture."), with its own ideas (a
  city skyline at night, a café counter by a window, a rooftop at golden hour) and its own price: **22 credits** (Crush 18,
  Soulmate 13; a photo is 15).
- Made by Nano Banana 2's edit model from its full body, 4:1 at 2K (about $0.12), then cut on our server with sharp to
  **exactly 1500 × 500** (its right part: the character about two thirds across, the lower left clear where X puts the
  profile picture), and 768 × 256 for its tile.
- On its page: a strip of its own, "X banners · 1500 × 500" (3:1 tiles, with a bar while one is made), never in its wall
  of photos and videos, and never among Explore's fresh photos (an X header, not a post). Seen big: "On X: your profile →
  Edit profile → tap the header picture, and pick this one." **Download** (a JPEG with the share mark, "<Name>-X-banner.jpg"),
  Share on X, Captions; never a video or a trend video from it (our server answers 409 `banner`).

**Captions** (the owner: "can gerate raedy made captions on their posts, or they can generate one too"):
- **Captions** in the sheet of one of its own done photos, banners, videos and trend videos, for X, TikTok or Instagram:
  **ready-made** (free and instant, in the page: `src/studio/captions.js`, 4 at a time, **More ideas** for the next 4) or
  **written by AI** in a tone (Funny, Flirty, Aesthetic, Hype, Wholesome): 3 at a time, free, **30 a day** per wallet ("29
  left today") and 3,000 a day for the whole site, counted in the database before the AI is asked.
- **Copy**, and for X **Post on X ↗**: X's own new-post box with the caption and a link to that creation (the visitor
  posts it, never us: hard rule 6). TikTok and Instagram: "download it first, then paste the caption as you post it".
- **Every caption** is PG-13, never about money, coins, prices or buying (whole words: `MONEY` in

  post shows (its scene, or its trend's name), never anything about the person.

**clank.trade usernames** (the owner: "i just saw theres a username system on clank.trade is it possible their username
in there would be in the studio as well when they connected there and their username will appear also on the studio?"):
- **My studio → Your clank.trade name:** type it once ("@name", "name" or the profile's link), **Show it**. clank.trade has
  no lookup by wallet, so our server reads that profile with clank.trade's own API (`profiles.byUsername`: public,
  read-only, the one its website uses) and keeps the name **only when that profile's wallet is the one signed in here**
  ("That profile's wallet isn't the one you connected here: connect that wallet, or use your own username."). Then "Shown
  as @name ↗", and **Remove it**.
- Shown as **"by @name ↗"** on its public influencers' pages (a link to its clank.trade profile, built from the name in
  the page: never a link our server passes on) and **"by @name"** in Explore's influencers; never on a private one. On an
  influencer's page without a name: "Show your clank.trade name here →" (to My studio's card).
- **Read again once a week** while it's shown (when its maker opens AGI Studio signed in): a profile that's gone, renamed
  or moved to another wallet takes it off; clank.trade not answering keeps it. One name per wallet, one wallet per name (a
  name another wallet proves later moves to that wallet).
- Kept: `agi1_inf_names` (a scrambled wallet code, the name, when it was last checked). The name is public on clank.trade.

**Its addresses** (all in `/api/launch`): POST `inf-caption` (`{ job, tone, platform }` → `{ captions, left, perDay }`),
`inf-name-set` (`{ name }`) and `inf-name-clear`; `?inf-info`'s `me.clank`, the `maker` of `?inf=` and `?inf-explore`'s
influencers (`{ name }` only: the page builds the link), each job's `created` and the answers' `now`; `inf-make` takes a
photo's `shape: 'banner'`.

**What's new in the database** (`supabase/influencers.sql`: 15 tables and 63 functions): `agi1_inf_names`,
`agi1_inf_caption_days` (each wallet code's AI captions a day, kept 2 days) and `agi1_inf_days.captions` (the site's);

starts from); `inf_get` and `inf_3d_list` say when things started; an influencer's page and Explore give its maker's name,
and Explore's fresh photos never an X banner.

    0.0005 ETH, the gas wallet 0.002 ETH; 0 = never), kept in the database; a new level shows at once.

    signed with PASS_SECRET). Then a balance under its level reaches the owner's chats (the studio's clock reads them
    every 30 minutes; each low one at most every 6 hours, with its top-up link), and so do new support tickets and
    reports (how many, and the Mod tools address: never what anyone wrote) at most every 5 minutes. `/stop` in that chat

  - **Balances to look at yourself:** Gemini (Google AI Studio → Billing), Google Cloud, Supabase, Vercel and Pinata,
    links only (no balance our server can read), and a link to Mod tools.
- **Team:** add someone by their wallet's address, a nickname (2 to 24 characters, never one that passes for the owner,

- **Content:** the spotlight of the week, the trend clips, the example pictures and the reports, as before.
- **Testing:** credits for testing (round 3).

**Mod tools** (`/studio/mod`, for the team: the owner, a mod or support; My studio shows them its link):
- **Tickets:** Waiting · Answered · Closed. A ticket opens as the team sees it: who it is (their influencers, their credits
  and whether they're banned), the messages (each of the team's answers with who wrote it), **Send answer** (they see it
  as "AGI Studio support"), **Close the ticket**, and for a mod **Ban its maker**.
- **Reports** (a mod and the owner): **Take it down** (or **Show again**), **It's fine**, or **Ban its maker**.
- **Bans** (a mod and the owner): why, by whom and when; **Lift the ban** (tap twice). Lifted ones under "Lifted".
- Its own alerts link: new tickets (and, for a mod, reports), at most every 5 minutes.

**Help & support** (`/studio/help`, from My studio, the footer and a ban's words):
- **The AI helper:** quick answers about AGI Studio, written by AI (the site's own Gemini key and chat model, its safety
  filters on) from our own guide (`helpGuide()` in `server/inf-help.js`: how things work, the prices, holder perks, how
  long things take, the rules; never an AI service's name), in the person's language. Anyone (signed out, after the human
  check): 20 answers a day each (a wallet, or a visitor's daily code), 600 a day for the site, 300 characters a question,
  with their one or two questions before it for a follow-up (never its answers). When a question needs a person (a payment
  that didn't arrive, something that failed, a ban, a bug) it says so, with **Open a ticket** on that topic. A seed phrase,
  a private key or a transaction's ID is never sent to the AI: the page says why (`HELP_SECRET`), and the question isn't
  put back in the box. "Answers are written by AI and can be wrong."
- **Your tickets** (a connected wallet): a topic (credits or a payment, something made or not made, my account or a ban,
  something broke, something else) and what happened (1,000 characters at most); 3 open at once, 20 messages a day, 500
  tickets a day for the site. A message with a seed phrase or a private key is refused before anything is kept (a
  transaction's link or ID is fine: "0x" and 64 characters). A new answer from the team: a dot on My studio (also said to
  screen readers) and "New answer" on the ticket. A ticket the team answered and nobody wrote in for 14 days closes
  itself; closed ones go after 90 days, with their messages.
- **What we never ask for:** a seed phrase, a private key or a password; to send money or tokens, sign anything or connect
  a wallet elsewhere; to move to a DM.
- `/help?new=<topic>` opens a new ticket about that (a ban's words use `?new=account`), `/help?ticket=<id>` one of yours.

**Bans** (a mod's or the owner's, from a report, a ticket or an influencer): the wallet that made an influencer, with a
reason (a real person who didn't agree, looked like a minor, sexual or too revealing, hate or harassment, violence or gore,
someone else's character or work, spam, a scam or pretending to be someone) and a note only the team sees. Then:

  gives its credits back; its credits stay;
- its influencers, their pictures and their videos are shown to nobody: Explore, likes, the spotlight, the stats board, their

  (its cards say "Hidden while banned"), and Create says so first;
- it can still open support tickets, buy credits and delete;
- the owner's and the team's wallets can't be banned. A mod or the owner lifts it, and everything comes back.

**How it works:** `server/inf-team.js` (who a wallet is: its role, its nickname and its ban, kept 20 s per server copy;

#### Round 4, phase 3 (2026-10-11): gifts of credits, gift links, invites

**The owner's picks** (items 3 and 2 of the list): **"gifting bought credits only"** (to a wallet, an @name or a gift link;
at most 50,000 credits a day) and **referrals for credits only** (a friend's 100 credits with its first top-up of $5 or more;
its inviter 10% of what the friend buys, at most 500 credits from one friend and 5,000 a month). Built while the owner
slept, tested and saved here; nothing goes live until the owner's steps below.

**Bonus credits**, a third kind next to bought ones and this month's free ones:
- What's bonus: an invite's rewards (a friend's welcome credits, an inviter's 10%) and, since this phase, the owner's credits
  for testing (round 3's gift: they counted as bought ones before).
- Spent after this month's free ones and before bought ones (free → bonus → bought), and given back the same way when
  something can't be made; they never run out, and they're **never given as a gift** (only bought ones are).
- My studio's Credits card says what they're made of: "100 credits of them are this month's free ones (used first; they
  end with the month).", "60 credits are bonus credits, from invites or the team (used next; they don't run out, and can't
  be given).", "2,240 credits you bought or got as gifts: those you can give."

**Giving credits** (My studio → **Gifts and invites** → **Give to a wallet**):
- **Who it's for:** a wallet's address (mixed case must be its checksum, so a typo is caught; never the zero or the burn
  address, never itself), or the clank.trade name it shows here ("@name", "name" or its profile's link: only a name a wallet
  proved in AGI Studio, round 4's names).
- **How many:** only credits it bought (or got as gifts), from 10 a gift, up to 50,000 a day (`STUDIO_GIFTS_A_DAY`) and 20
  gifts a day (gift links included); a few amounts to tap, never more than it has.
- **A note** (optional, 80 characters): kind words only: never a link, a contact, a deal (a price, "cheap", "sell", a payment,
  a place to talk elsewhere: a gift is never a sale), a seed phrase or a private key, or crude words.
- **A review before anything moves:** "Give 250 credits to @nova_maker?", its note, and "Once it's given it's theirs: a gift
  to a wallet can't be taken back. Check who it's for.", then **Give 250 credits** (or **Change**, everything as typed).
  Every "no", the page's or our server's, is said under its own field, with the keyboard there.
- Given: "Given: 250 credits to @nova_maker 💜". They're the other wallet's own bought credits (to use, or to give on).

**Gift links** (**Make a gift link**): how many (the same rules) and a note, then its link,
`…/explore#gift=<its secret>`, to copy (or share from a phone's own share sheet). Its credits are held until someone claims
it once: "It can be claimed until <date>" (30 days; then they come back by themselves, with the studio's clock); 10 waiting
at most. Its row in the card: **Copy link**, and **Take it back** while nobody has claimed it (two taps: the first asks "Tap
again to take it back" and is forgotten after 6 s).
- **Its secret is the part after "#gift=":** a page's address never carries it to a server (a fragment stays in the
  browser); it goes only in a POST's body (`inf-gift-peek`, `inf-gift-claim`), and the page takes it out of its address as
  soon as its sheet closes. Anyone with the link can claim it: the page says to keep it to yourself.
- **Opening one** (anyone, signed in or not): "A gift for you", how many, from whom (its clank.trade name, else its short
  address), its note, until when and "A connected wallet (a free signature) and 18+", then **Claim 300 credits** (18+, then
  the wallet sheet if no wallet is connected). Claimed: "💜 300 credits are yours" and **Make something**. Claimed already,
  taken back, expired or broken: said, with **Explore AGI Studio**. Its sender can't claim its own.
- **On a phone without a wallet** (Safari, Chrome): "No wallet in this browser? Copy this gift link, then open it in your
  wallet app's own browser (MetaMask, Phantom, Coinbase Wallet, or Robinhood Wallet's Web3 tab) and claim it there. Keep it
  to yourself: anyone with the link can claim it." with **Copy the gift link**. The wallet sheet's "Open in …" links never
  carry the secret (their addresses go to those apps' own servers), and while a gift link is open it says so: "copy the gift
  link first". (Found while building the browser test: the first version left a phone with nothing to claim with.)
- **A gift a wallet got** (sent to it): a toast once ("💜 You got a gift: 250 credits. See it in My studio."), never on My
  studio, which lists them, "New" on each until it's been seen. A link it claimed itself is seen already.

**Invites** (the same card):
- Each wallet's own invite link, `…/explore?ref=<code>` (8 letters and numbers, never 0, 1, i, l or o), **Copy**, **Share on
  X ↗** (X's own post box: the visitor posts), what an invite brings, and how its invites went (friends joined, friends who
  bought credits, its rewards this month out of 5,000, in all).
- **Someone opens it:** its code is kept in that browser (30 days at most) and taken out of the page's address at once;
  signed out, a toast says what joining brings ("connect a wallet, and your first top-up of $5 or more brings 100 bonus
  credits"). Once a wallet signs in, it joins with it: only a wallet that never bought credits, once, never with its own code
  or the code of a wallet it invited ("joined through an invite" in a toast); a "no" that won't change (its own code, bought
  already…) drops the code quietly.
- Or typed in My studio's "Got an invite code?" (a wallet that never bought credits: the code, or the whole link).
- **Its welcome:** Buy credits says it first ("You joined through an invite 💜 100 bonus credits come with your first top-up
  of $5 or more."), and its first top-up of $5 or more brings them ("Payment found: 600 credits added, and your invite's 100
  bonus credits 💜").
- **Its inviter's reward:** 10% of each of its friend's top-ups as bonus credits (at most 500 from one friend in all, 5,000 a
  month for each inviter; only top-ups after the friend joined), counted once each: right after the top-up ("Check my
  payment"), and by the studio's clock every 30 minutes for anything missed. Rows in the card: "From a friend you invited
  +60", "Welcome credits from your invite +100".

**A banned wallet** can't give, claim or join (`BANNED_FROM`; its card says "A banned wallet can't give or claim gifts, or
invite anyone."); **its gift links wait** while the ban lasts (nobody can claim them: a ban for selling credits stops its
links too), and work again once it's lifted; taking its own link back still works. Its invites bring nothing while it's
banned (a banned friend gets no welcome credits, a banned inviter no 10%).

**Switched off:** `STUDIO_GIFTS=off`: no giving and no gift links (a gift link says gifts are off; links already made wait,
and their senders can still take them back). `STUDIO_REFERRALS=off`: no invites (no links, joining or rewards). With both
off, My studio has no card. **While AGI Studio is private**, giving waits ("Giving opens when AGI Studio opens to
everyone."); claiming and invites work.

**How it works:** `server/inf-gifts.js` (who a gift is for, its note, sending, a link made, seen, claimed or taken back, a
wallet's gifts and rewards, invite codes, joining, settling rewards), its actions in `/api/launch` (`inf-gifts`, `inf-send`,
`inf-gift-link`, `inf-gift-cancel`, `inf-gift-claim`, `inf-ref-bind`, and `inf-gift-peek` for anyone), rewards settled after
a top-up (`server/credits.js`) and by the clock (`server/inf-jobs.js`); the page: `src/studio/views/gifts.js` (the card, the
give sheet, the gift link sheet, a gift link's own sheet), `app.js` (invite links and gift links in the address, joining
once a wallet signs in, a gift's toast, the welcome in Buy credits), `me.js` (the card, credits by kind); the rules in
`src/studio/rules.js` (`GIFTS`, `REFERRALS`, `REF_CODE`, `GIFT_TOKEN`, `inviteLink()`, `giftLink()`) and the words in
`app-words.js`. The AI helper's guide knows them.

**What's new in the database** (`supabase/influencers.sql`: 27 tables and 93 functions): `agi1_credit_gifts` (each gift:
scrambled codes of both wallets and how the page shows them, its credits, note, status and whether its recipient saw it; a
gift link's secret, kept with its gift so an old link can say what became of it; a gift that's done goes a year later),
`agi1_inf_refs` (each wallet's invite code), `agi1_inf_invited` (who joined through whom, its welcome, what it earned its
inviter), `agi1_inf_ref_months` (an inviter's rewards a month: its cap), `agi1_inf_ref_paid` (each friend's top-up counted
once); `agi1_credits.bonus`, and in the credits' log each spend's bonus part and a gift's other side; 9 functions
(`inf_send`, `inf_gift_link`, `inf_gift_peek`, `inf_gift_claim`, `inf_gift_cancel`, `inf_gifts_mine`, `inf_ref_code`,
`inf_ref_bind`, `inf_ref_settle`), and the round 3 gift (`inf_gift`) now bonus credits.

**Fixed while testing it:** a gift note that held a seed phrase was refused as "too long" when it was (its own warning now,
first); the safety note said a gift link's secret was kept only "until the link is claimed, taken back or expires" (it stays
with its gift: corrected, and tested); and the phone without a wallet, above.

**Owner, in this order:**
1. **Supabase** → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/influencers.sql` → Run → `influencers_ready = 1`.
   **Before pushing:** the new code needs its new functions (with the version before it, the card and a gift link say "AGI
   Studio isn't open yet.", and the log names the fix).
2. **Push.** Optional settings (Vercel, then Redeploy): `STUDIO_GIFTS` = `off`, `STUDIO_GIFTS_A_DAY` (50,000),
   `STUDIO_REFERRALS` = `off`, `STUDIO_REF_WELCOME` (100), `STUDIO_REF_PERCENT` (10), `STUDIO_REF_PER_FRIEND` (500),
   `STUDIO_REF_A_MONTH` (5,000).
3. Try it with two wallets: a gift link from yours, claimed in the other; your invite link opened by a wallet that never
   bought credits, then its first top-up of $5.

**Cost:** nothing new to pay. Bonus credits cost what they're spent on (fal's balance, like the owner's credits for testing):
a friend's 100 welcome credits once, after it pays $5 or more, and its inviter's 10% of what it buys (at most 500 credits from
one friend, 5,000 a month for each inviter). Gifts move credits that were already bought.

**Troubleshooting** (Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Logs):

#### Giving access while it's private (2026-10-11)

**The owner:** "i want to give access to someone but it said to them comins soon fix that please". While AGI Studio is private,
only the wallets in Vercel's `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR` could make anything, and everyone else read "AGI Studio is private for now: it
opens to everyone soon" (the "coming soon" the friend saw). The quick way out that day (adding the friend's wallet to
`STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`, then Redeploy) still works; this makes it one tap, with no Vercel and no Redeploy.

**What the owner sees** (Owner tools → **Testing**, above credits for testing; `accessSection()` in `views/owner.js`):
- **Who can use AGI Studio:** its first line says who's in without the list ("Also in, without the list: you, your team (2
  people) and 1 wallet in STUDIO_ONLY_FOR in Vercel (0x2222…2222).", or that it's open to everyone with `STUDIO_OPEN`), then
  the list, newest first: each wallet's short address, the owner's note, "Let in by you" or "Got credits for testing", since
  when, "on your team too", and **Take off** (a second tap: "Tap again to take off", forgotten after 5 s).
- **Give someone access:** their wallet's address (the one they'll connect: they can copy it from My studio) and a note if the
  owner likes (24 characters, only the owner sees it), **Give access** → "0x6666…6666 can use AGI Studio now 💜 They connect
  that wallet and reload the page." The same wallet again changes its note ("was on the list already: its note is saved").
  Every "no" under the form, with the keyboard back on its box: not an address, the owner's own wallet ("it's always in"), a
  note too long, the list full (200).
- **Credits for testing let a tester in:** giving credits to a tester's wallet while AGI Studio is private puts it on the
  list too ("Added 1,000 credits to 0x7777…7777 💜 It can use AGI Studio now too: it's on your list above."), as "Got credits
  for testing". A wallet already on it stays as it was; one the list couldn't take (full, or an older `influencers.sql`) is
  said ("…that wallet can't use them yet: give it access in "Who can use AGI Studio" above."). Never in Vercel any more.

**What the friend sees** (a connected wallet that isn't on the list, while it's private): Explore and Create: "AGI Studio is
private for now, and this wallet isn't on its list yet. Invited? Send whoever invited you this wallet's address (it's in My
studio), then reload once you're in. Or follow @agi1dotapp on X to hear when it opens to everyone." My studio: "AGI Studio is
private for now, and this wallet isn't on its list yet.", "Invited? Send this wallet's address to whoever invited you. Once
they've let it in, reload this page.", their whole address with **Copy address**, and "Not invited? Follow @agi1dotapp on X to
hear when it opens to everyone." Never "opens soon" (that's only for a studio that isn't set up). Signed out: nothing about the
list (it can't know the wallet yet). Let in, a reload and it's theirs.

**How it works:**
- **Who may use it** (`canUse()` in `server/inf-team.js`, at every gate that used `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR` alone: starting an
  influencer, its uploads, buying credits, giving credits, a burn's quote, a clank.trade name, `inf-me`'s `allowed`): open to
  everyone (`STUDIO_OPEN`), or on its list (`onList()`): the owner's wallet, `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`'s, the team's (mods and
  support), or a wallet the owner let in. Read with the team's `whoIs()` (kept 20 s per server copy: a friend let in a moment
  ago may need a second reload on another copy), so it costs no extra database call. The database away, or an
  `influencers.sql` older than this: only the owner's and `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`'s (fail closed), said once in the log.
- **A coin link while launching is private** (`LAUNCH_ONLY_FOR`): AGI Studio's own list gets one (the owner,
  `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`'s, the team, the wallets let in), never everyone just because AGI Studio is open.
- **The owner's actions** (`/api/launch`, the owner's tools' checks): `inf-access` (the list, and who's in without it),
  `inf-access-set` (`address`, `note`), `inf-access-remove` (`code`).

**What's kept** (`agi1_inf_access` in `supabase/influencers.sql`, only the server's key): per wallet let in its scrambled code
(never the address), its short address ("0x12ab…cdef", to tell them apart), the owner's note, how it got in and when; taken off,
it's deleted. The safety note's 04 and AGI Studio's own "What's kept" say so.

**Owner, in this order:**
1. **Supabase** → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/influencers.sql` → Run → `influencers_ready = 1` (28
   tables, 96 functions). **Before pushing:** the new code reads who's on the list from it (with the version before it, the
   list says to run it again, and nobody gets in but you, `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`'s and your team).
2. **Push.**
3. Owner tools → **Testing** → **Who can use AGI Studio** → paste the friend's wallet address (they copy it from My studio) →
   **Give access**. They reload the page. To let someone go: **Take off** (two taps).

**Cost:** nothing.

**Troubleshooting** (Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Logs):

| What you see | Log line | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Run supabase/influencers.sql again in Supabase first…" on the Testing tab | `[studio] the studio app: inf_access_list not found: run supabase/influencers.sql again in this Supabase project (giving access from the owner's tab; …)` | Owner step 1, then Try again |
| A friend let in still reads "private for now" | (none) | They reload once more after a few seconds (a server copy keeps who's who 20 s), with the same wallet they sent you |
| Nobody but you and `STUDIO_ONLY_FOR`'s get in | `[studio] couldn't read who may use AGI Studio (only STUDIO_ONLY_FOR's wallets for now): …` | The database (a paused Supabase project: resume it), or `influencers.sql` not run again |
| "The list is full (200 wallets)" | (none) | Take someone off, or open AGI Studio to everyone (`STUDIO_OPEN`) |

### AGI Studio's guide (2026-10-11)

**The owner's request:** "theres should be a video guide on the site on every step and arrows so they dont get confused
everyone gets that ofcourse they have an option to X IT but put vosials and video on the guidses please". The owner's choice:
**"Guide next (Recommended)"** (before the meme templates): arrows that walk through each step on the real buttons, an ✕ to
close, and a short video for each step, recorded from the real app (never drawn or made by AI). Built the same day, tested
and saved here; nothing goes live until the owner pushes it.

**What visitors see** (`src/studio/guide.js`; the guides and their steps in `src/studio/guide-steps.js`):
- **A guide on each page that needs one:** Explore (where to start, the gallery, your wallet or your credits, the bar, the
  ? button), Create (how to start, its look or its photo, style, outfit and vibe, its name, Create), an influencer's looks
  (pick one; 4 new looks), its tools (what to make, the scene, the model, Make, Instant, your creations) and My studio (your
  wallet or your credits, your influencers, gifts and invites, Help & support): 25 steps. A step shows only when it fits the
  page as it is (signed in or out, designed or from a photo, Instant on or off), and one whose button isn't on the page is
  passed.
- **Each step:** a card beside the step's real button, an arrow pointing at it and a ring around it (the rest of the page a
  little dimmer, still usable); "2 of 6", its title and its words; a short muted video of that step being done in the real
  app (a computer's recording on a computer, a phone's on a phone), with a pause button; **Back**, **Next** (**Done** on the
  last), **✕**, and **Skip all guides**. A computer: the card beside its button (right, then left), else under or over it.
  A phone: the card the width of the screen, under its button or over it, never covering it while there's room; a step in
  the drawer of controls opens the drawer first ("Your creations" closes it). The page scrolls its button into view first
  (a computer: in the middle when the card fits beside it, else near the top with the card under it; a phone: near the
  top), and the card follows it if the page moves. **A card never covers its button for its video:** when the card with its
  video can't fit beside, under or over its button (a short screen, a button at the end of what scrolls), it goes without
  its video and shows **Watch how** instead, which shows it (playing, over its button then: they asked).
- **When:** by itself the first time this browser opens that page, once the page is ready (no sheet open, the tab shown, its
  first button there); never again by itself after that, however it was closed. The **?** in the top bar ("Show me around
  this page") shows the page's guide again from its first step (on a page without one, it opens Learn; on Learn it's hidden).
  Learn's **Show me with arrows** opens a page with `?guide=1`, its guide at once (the address is tidied right after). **Skip
  all guides**: none starts by itself again in this browser ("Guides are off. Tap ? on any page to see one."). ✕ and Escape
  close it; it goes when the page changes, and hides while a sheet is open.
- **Kept in this browser only** (`agi_guide`: which guides were seen, and "Skip all guides"); nothing is sent anywhere. A
  private window or blocked storage: a guide may show again on the next visit, nothing worse.
- **Its videos:** muted and soundless; nothing is downloaded until a step shows (`preload="none"`, its poster first). They
  play by themselves while they're shown, unless the visitor asked for "reduce motion" or the browser asks to save data
  (then the poster, with a play button), never out of sight. A browser that can't play them (rare: they're H.264, which
  Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox play) hides the box of the one it tried, and shows the next ones' posters. Each is 4.5
  to 13 seconds and 45 to 465 KB (a whole guide's videos are about 1.3 MB at most).
- **The keyboard and screen readers:** the card's title takes the keyboard when a guide starts; ← and → step, Escape closes
  it; each step is said by a live region; the video is decoration (its words say the same). Back to the page's main part
  when it closes.
- **The first-time tips are gone** (round 4, phase 4's line on Explore, Create and My studio): the guide does their job.
- **Learn** (`/learn`): each lesson with its video (its steps' videos from the guide, one after the other, never playing by
  itself there) and **Show me with arrows** where a page has a guide; "On any page, tap ? at the top for its guide with
  arrows."
- **The AI helper** knows the guide (`helpGuide()` in `server/inf-help.js`: "THE GUIDE AND LEARN"), and its "MAKING
  THINGS" line knows round 4's phase 4 (the model menu, memes, references, Long videos, Anime, Instant), which it had missed.

**How it works:** each page names what its arrows point at (`data-guide` on its buttons and sections: `start`, `gallery`,
`account`, `nav`, `guide` (the ? button), `mode`, `look`, `style`, `name`, `go`, `looks`, `reroll`, `tools`, `scene`,
`models`, `instant`, `creations`, `connect`, `credits`, `mine`, `gifts`, `help`), and offers its guide through `ctx.guide(id,
env)` in `src/studio/app.js` (what the page is like now, and how to open and close a phone's drawer). The card is made with
`createElement` and its words set as text; its places only through the CSS object model (the CSP forbids style attributes);
every rule names an `sa-guide` class (`src/styles/studio-app.css`). The videos come from our own address (Vite gives each its
own name, kept a year by browsers): the CSP is unchanged (`media-src 'self' blob:`).

**The videos** (`src/studio/guide/`, listed in `src/studio/guide-media.js`; made by `tools/studio/guide-record.mjs`, their
scenes in `tools/studio/guide-scripts.mjs`):
- **26 videos** (every step's, and two more for Learn: a trend video and a video being made), each twice: a computer's (672
  × 420, filmed on a 1280 × 800 screen) and a phone's (624 × 390, filmed on a 390 × 844 phone, with touches): 16:10, 24
  frames a second, soundless H.264 MP4s with WebP posters. 104 files, about 10 MB.
- **Filmed from the real app:** AGI Studio as Vite builds it, in Chromium, with our own server's code answering it
  (`api/launch.js`) and its outside services faked exactly as `tests/influencer.test.js` fakes them (read from that file as it
  runs). A demo studio: made-up people from the live show's 2D paintings (`tools/live/page/art`: never anyone real, never the
  3D model or anything rendered from it), their photos and videos made from those paintings, a made-up wallet with demo
  credits. Each scene scripted (what's clicked, typed and tapped, and when), a cursor (a computer's) or a touch (a phone's)
  drawn on top, and a camera that follows what happens (a 16:10 part of the screen), a little faster where the app waits.
  Frames from Chromium's own screencast, put together with sharp, encoded with ffmpeg.
- **Never** a secret (the browser and ffmpeg get none), another site (only the app's own address, which stands in as
  https://studio.agi1.app), the 3D model, or a real person. A guide card in a video shows its words and arrows only (the app
  being filmed has no videos of its own).
- **Made again** by Claude after a page with a guide changes how it looks (see "Commands"); `tests/guide.test.js` fails the
  build if a step's video is missing, too long, too big or not a real soundless MP4.

**Owner:** push. No SQL, no setting, nothing on the live show's server. **Cost:** nothing to pay: about 10 MB more in the
repo and its builds; each visitor downloads only the videos of the steps they see (from Vercel's CDN, inside its bandwidth).

**Troubleshooting:**

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A page's guide doesn't start by itself | This browser has seen it (or "Skip all guides" was pressed) | Tap ? in the top bar |
| A step's video doesn't match the page | The page changed after its video was filmed | Tell Claude: the recorder films it again |
| The video is a still picture | "Reduce motion" is on, or the browser asks to save data | Tap its play button |
| A step shows "Watch how" instead of its video | The card with its video would cover its button there (a short screen, the end of a page) | Tap Watch how |
| A step is left out | Its button isn't on the page as it is (signed out, Instant on, the photo way) | Nothing to fix |

**Tests:** `tests/guide.test.js` (10: each page's steps, their buttons on the pages, their words and videos and when they
show; what's kept in this browser; where a step's card goes, its ring, and how much of its button a card would cover

## CloakMesh at inference.agi1.app (2026-10-03)

**The owner's project:** CloakMesh, "a Zero-Gateway P2P confidential AI inference network", whose Phase 1 Claude built in
the owner's `CloakMesh` folder on the Desktop (a Rust library for the client and the server side, and a Python privacy
filter; see that folder's README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md). The owner: "It will be put on inference.agi1.app", then "Landing
page first": an explainer and a free waitlist, on this site. The network itself isn't live yet (no servers).

**What visitors see** (`cloakmesh.html`, `src/cloakmesh/`, `src/styles/cloakmesh.css`):
- Its own serious look, light and dark (the visitor's choice, else their device's setting; `/cloakmesh-theme.js` before the
  page paints, remembered as `cm-theme`), its own top bar (CloakMesh "by AGI", How it works · Demo · Proof · FAQ, the theme
  button, Join the waitlist; on phones just the button, "Join") and footer ("A project of AGI", the trademark line).
  Nothing of AGI-1, Pop mode or the coin.
- The top: "Private AI, with nothing in the middle." and a card: what you type → what leaves your device (tokens) → the
  checks. Then how it works (3 steps), the demo, who sees what (a table), the five checks ("How your device knows it's
  real": their numbers light up one by one as they come into view; with "reduce motion", lit from the start), the
  difference (through a gateway vs. CloakMesh: **no company named**, the owner's rule), speed (the benchmark's numbers, with
  how they were measured), what Phase 1 doesn't do yet, questions, the waitlist.
- **The demo** ("See what leaves your device", `src/cloakmesh/demo.js`): a small version of CloakMesh's filter, **only in the
  visitor's browser** (no network call, nothing kept: `tests/cloakmesh.test.js` checks the file): names after a cue
  ("I'm…", "Dear…", "Dr."), email addresses, phone numbers, cards (their network, length and the Luhn check), IBANs (mod-97),
  ID numbers, passwords after a cue, API keys, private keys, seed phrases after a cue, wallet addresses and keys, IP
  addresses. Each becomes `[CATEGORY_CODE]` (HMAC-SHA256 under a key made for the visit, base32: the real filter's tokens);
  then a made-up answer written with the tokens only, and the same answer with them put back. Its text box has the
  browser's spellcheck off (a spellcheck service could otherwise see what's typed). It says it's simplified, and asks for
  made-up details anyway.
- **Honest on purpose:** "Phase 1 built", "not live yet", GPUs are Phase 2, the filter is pattern-based, the speed numbers
  say how they were measured (the handshake on simulated hardware). Never "open source", "audited" or "guaranteed" (a test
  checks), never another company's name, never $AGI.

**The waitlist** (`api/cloakmesh.js`, `server/cloakmesh.js`, `supabase/cloakmesh.sql`):
- An email address, and what they'd mostly like to do: use it, build on it, run a server (`use`, `build`, `node`). The
  human check (Turnstile, action `waitlist`, and the chat's 2-hour pass), 10 tries a minute per visitor, 5 sign-ups a day
  per visitor (a daily code of their internet address, never the address), 2,000 a day for the site.
- **Kept:** the address (lowercase), the pick and the day; nothing else (no internet address, no time of day). Row level
  security on, only the server's key.
- **A leave link** for each person: `…/cloakmesh#leave=<64 hex characters>` (made by the database; after the `#`, so it never
  reaches a server's logs; the page takes it out of the address at once). It shows "Leave the CloakMesh waitlist?", and one
  button deletes the row for good.
- **Nobody can learn who joined:** the same answer (and the same link) whether or not an address was already on the list.
- **No email is sent** (that needs an email service: the owner's decision). So addresses aren't confirmed: someone could
  add someone else's address, who can leave with the link in the first email (see "Open questions").
- Nothing logs an email address, a leave code or an internet address.

**How inference.agi1.app works:** `vercel.json` redirects `inference.agi1.app/` to `/cloakmesh` (a 307, so it can change
later). Not a rewrite: Vercel serves the home page's own file (`index.html`) at "/" before any rewrite runs (its docs:
"precedence is given to the filesystem prior to rewrites being applied"), so a rewrite would show the AGI-1 site. Other
addresses on inference.agi1.app show the site's other pages (nobody links there). The page's canonical address and link
preview say https://inference.agi1.app/cloakmesh. Cloudflare's human check already works there: a widget's hostname covers
its subdomains (Cloudflare's docs), and agi1.app is on the widget.

**Setup (the owner, once; free):**
1. **The domain:** Vercel → agi-ecosystem → Settings → **Domains** → **Add Domain** → `inference.agi1.app` → Add. Vercel
   shows a DNS record to add (a CNAME). agi1.app's DNS is Namecheap's web hosting DNS (its nameservers are
   dns1/dns2.namecheaphosting.com, checked 2026-10-03), so the record goes in that hosting account's **cPanel → Zone
   Editor** (Namecheap's own guide), not Domain List → Advanced DNS: name `inference`, type CNAME, the value Vercel shows.
   Then wait until Vercel says "Valid Configuration".
2. **The database:** Supabase → the same project → SQL Editor → New query → paste **all** of `supabase/cloakmesh.sql` → Run.
   It ends with `cloakmesh_functions_found = 3`. Until then the page says the waitlist opens soon.
3. **Push** (a branch first, as usual: its preview link shows the page at /cloakmesh), then check https://inference.agi1.app
   on a phone and a computer: the page, the demo, joining with your own email, your leave link.
No new settings: it uses the site's Supabase, Turnstile and PASS_SECRET.

**Status (2026-10-03):** the owner pushed it (to `main`, with everything else in the folder) and ran
`supabase/cloakmesh.sql`: https://agi1.app/cloakmesh is live and `/api/cloakmesh` says `{"ready":true}` (Claude
checked). inference.agi1.app waits: the owner's Namecheap account is temporarily suspended, so its record can't be added
yet. Until it works, **don't share the page's link**: its link preview and canonical address point at
inference.agi1.app (Claude can point them at agi1.app for a while if the owner wants to share it sooner). Leave links
made meanwhile use agi1.app/cloakmesh, which keeps working after the domain is added.

**Reading the list:** Supabase → Table Editor → `agi1_cloakmesh_waitlist` (Export → CSV). How many:
`select role, count(*) from agi1_cloakmesh_waitlist group by role;` For an email to everyone, with each person's own leave
link: `select email, role, joined, 'https://inference.agi1.app/cloakmesh#leave=' || leave_token as leave_link from
agi1_cloakmesh_waitlist order by id;` Someone asks to be removed without their link:
`delete from agi1_cloakmesh_waitlist where email = 'their@address';` (lowercase).

**Cost:** nothing new: Supabase (two small tables), Vercel (one small function, the 12th: see "Free-tier budgets"), and
about 25 KB of code and styles (gzipped) for each visitor, plus the site's font.

**Troubleshooting:**

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| inference.agi1.app shows the AGI-1 site | The redirect in `vercel.json` is missing | Put it back (`tests/cloakmesh.test.js` checks it) |
| inference.agi1.app doesn't open | The domain isn't set up (Vercel → Domains: "Invalid Configuration") | Add the DNS record Vercel shows (in Namecheap: the hosting account's cPanel → Zone Editor) |
| "The waitlist opens soon." | `supabase/cloakmesh.sql` isn't run (log: `[cloakmesh] … run supabase/cloakmesh.sql`), or the site's settings are missing | Setup step 2 |
| "We couldn't confirm you're human." | Cloudflare's human check failed | As the chat's (see "The chat's cost, setup and troubleshooting") |
| "The waitlist is very busy today." | 2,000 sign-ups today (`WAITLIST.SITE_DAILY` in `server/cloakmesh.js`) | Good news: tell Claude to raise it |
| A deployment fails: "No more than 12 Serverless Functions…" | Vercel's Hobby plan allows 12; `api/cloakmesh.js` is the 12th | Never a 13th file in `api/`: share one, or Vercel Pro ($20 a month) |

**Tests:** `tests/cloakmesh.test.js` (17: email addresses, `/api/cloakmesh` (open or not, its checks before anything is asked,
the human check made for `waitlist`, the leave link, the same answer for an address already there, nothing logged, the
limits, the database missing or down, leaving), the SQL's promises, the demo (what it finds, what it leaves alone, its
tokens checked against Node's own HMAC, every text put back, its answer, fast on 2,000 characters of the worst cases, never
sending or keeping anything), the page (its promises, no inline code, every link, its link preview), its scoped styles, its
words, inference.agi1.app's redirect, the 12-function limit). The SQL ran in PGlite (28 checks: bad input never kept, one
row per address, the same link, the daily limits, old counts deleted, leaving and joining again, running it twice, the
original site's tables untouched, permissions, row level security). In a browser with the site's real headers (120 checks:
both themes and remembering, the demo (tokens, nothing sent while typing, HTML stays text), the checks lighting up and
"reduce motion", the waitlist (every answer, the leave link, Copy, the pass), leaving (a broken link too), 1440 / 1024 / 390 / 360 / 320 px, axe 0
issues, the keyboard, clean consoles, no CSP violations).

**Next, the owner's decisions:** the pilot server (Google Cloud N2D with SEV-SNP, about $135 a month, a small open model on
its processor: roughly 50–100 people a day with a ~3B model, 20–30 with ~8B; Claude can prepare it for free first), sending
emails, pricing, and $AGI (the owner's choice, 2026-10-03: not on CloakMesh for now; later maybe a holder perk like early
access, never staking or paying holders).

## Pop mode (2026-09-27)

**The owner's request:** a button beside the dark / light button that switches the whole design of the page to the look
of the $AGI ecosystem page (then at https://www.agi1.app/), with the same contents, "turn off on default, you decide".
That page was the same brand, so Pop mode dresses this site in that family's look. (Since 2026-09-28 agi1.app is this site
itself; the ecosystem page it copied is gone, the look lives on here.)

**What visitors see:**
- A round **✦** button next to the theme button (both pages; the tooltip says "Pop mode: the bold AGI look"; "the AGI ecosystem look" until 2026-09-28). **On by
  default since 2026-09-28, in the dark theme** (the owner: "make the pop mode open on default, in dark mode"; before that
  it was off by default and the theme followed the system setting). Pressed, the page switches to the lab look; pressed
  again, back to Pop mode. Remembered in the browser (`dr-skin` = `pop` or `lab`), like the theme (`dr-theme`). The theme button still works inside it (Pop mode has a night version). On phones under
  380 px the top bar has no room for a fourth round button, so there it's a **"Pop mode On / Off"** row at the bottom of the
  menu (the menu stays open when it's tapped).
- **The same content:** every word, link, number, button and feature stays; only the CSS changes (`src/styles/pop.css`,
  every rule under `[data-skin="pop"]`, checked by a test). The one addition is decoration: two tilted ribbons between the
  hero and Evaluations that scroll phrases already on the page ("AGI ✦ Artificial Girlfriend Intelligence ♥
  AGI-1 ✦ Texts back instantly ♥ PG-13 ✦ Not financial advice", "Introducing AGI ♥ Zero red flags ✦ Your ex: 3 business days
  ♥ Robinhood Chain ✦ One official contract"), hidden from screen readers.
- **The look** (agi1.app's design language): ink outlines (`#170a36`) on paper (`#f8f5ff`) and lavender (`#e4d9ff`); each
  section a bold color block: the hero **violet** (`#6b3bff`) with comic speed lines and halftone dots, Evaluations **honey**
  (`#ffc933`), Model card paper, Playground **lavender**, ClankChecker **mint** (`#3ff0c3`) with a faint grid (the Arena's
  **pink** block left with it), the safety note **ink**, the bottom bar violet with "AGI" in huge type. Headings and big
  numbers in the wide **Anybody** type (weight 850–900), the hero's subtitle and the diary entries in **Instrument Serif**
  italics, mono uppercase eyebrows with a dot, pill buttons and chips with 2 px outlines, white cards with 3 px ink outlines
  and hard offset shadows (like stickers), AGI-1's stage and her live views as **pink comic panels** (her hearts there white,
  violet and honey; the 3D stage switches its floor-line colors), chat bubbles (hers lavender, yours violet), "Introducing
  AGI" in lavender with a pink offset shadow, a honey "Try AGI-1" in the hero.
- **At night** (the dark theme): a deep violet hero and stage, deep ink sections, each keeping its color as an accent (the
  eyebrow dot and its cards' shadows: honey, blue, violet, mint), honey buttons and focus rings.
- **The top bar:** floating pills over the hero (the wordmark, the section links in one white pill, round buttons). Once the
  hero has scrolled away (on the diary page: once the page scrolls at all) it gets a **frosted band** with an ink line under
  it (`is-stuck`, added by `src/menu.js`), so the pills never sit on busy text. The pills need about 1,000 px in one line,
  so in Pop mode the menu takes over up to **1040 px** (a card under the pills); the default look's menu starts at 960 px
  (920 px until the Telegram button, 2026-10-05: with it the pills need about 1,020 px, still 20 px to spare at 1041).
- The phone's browser bar: violet at the top of the home page (deep violet at night), the page's own color on the diary
  (and since 2026-10-01 on the launch page).
- The keyboard's focus ring: violet on the light blocks, white on the violet hero, ink in the top bar and on her pink
  stage (and since 2026-10-02 on her live view's buttons, where violet didn't stand out on her pink panel), honey on the ink footer and
  everywhere at night.
- **Switching keeps your place** (2026-09-27, the owner: "why when i click pop mode it goes to a different section of the
  page?"). Pop mode's sections are taller and its headlines bigger, and a browser keeps the number of pixels scrolled, not
  what you were reading: switching halfway down the page showed another section (270 to 2,270 px away, measured). Browsers'
  own "scroll anchoring" doesn't help here (it steps aside when the spacing of sections changes; older Safaris have none).
  Now `keepPlace()` in `src/theme.js`, before a switch, notes what's in the middle of the screen (the innermost paragraph,
  card, row or chat box there; never the top bar, its menu or her live view strip, which stay put on the screen) and exactly
  which point of it; after the switch it scrolls at once so that point is back in the same spot, and once more when Pop
  mode's two fonts have arrived (they make its headlines bigger), unless the visitor scrolled or pressed something meanwhile.
  At the very top of the page it stays at the top. The theme button does the same (Pop mode's night look has thinner
  outlines). What's in the middle stays; what's above it may grow or shrink.

**How it works:** `/theme.js` (a tiny script in `<head>`) puts `data-skin="pop"` on `<html>` before the page paints unless
the browser saved `dr-skin` = `lab` (Pop mode switched off), and `data-theme="dark"` unless it saved `dr-theme` = `light`
(the system setting doesn't decide any more), so the page never flashes the other look. `src/theme.js` wires the buttons (every
`[data-skin-toggle]`, with `aria-pressed`), remembers the choice, repaints the browser bar (`barColor()`, the same colors as
`/theme.js`; a test compares them) and sends `agi:skin`; the 3D stage listens (its `pop-light` / `pop-dark` colors, the
hearts) and so does the menu (it closes when its links fit again). Browsers keep `/theme.js` a
day, so the pages load it with a version (`/theme.js?v=6` since her pop-out window, 2026-10-02, `v=5` since full-screen talk, `v=4` since the launch page, `v=3` since the front: **raise the number whenever it changes**)
and `src/theme.js` also applies the saved choices, else the same defaults (`DEFAULT_SKIN`, `DEFAULT_THEME`) itself.

**Fonts:** Anybody (variable, 57 KB) and Instrument Serif Italic (22 KB), free (SIL Open Font License, the license files are
next to them in `public/fonts/`), self-hosted like Geist (nothing from Google) and **only downloaded while Pop mode is on**
(since it's the default, most visitors download them: 79 KB). Browsers keep them a year (like Geist).

**Cost:** nothing: no new service, no new setting, no server work; only the two fonts, for Pop mode visitors, once.

**Also changed for everyone** (found while measuring the top bar for this): the menu now starts at 920 px (the new button made
the row of links about 40 px longer; it was 860), and the Arena's leaderboard folds each coin into two lines up to 920 px (at
901–904 px its Vote buttons stuck out 3 px).

**Troubleshooting:**

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No ✦ button on a phone | Under 380 px it's the "Pop mode" row at the bottom of the menu | Nothing to fix |
| Pop mode is on, but after a reload the lab look shows for a moment first | That browser still has yesterday's `/theme.js` (browsers keep it a day) | Nothing to fix: the page switches as it loads, and before the first paint from the next day |
| A new section or feature looks plain in Pop mode | New markup needs its Pop mode styles in `src/styles/pop.css` | Tell Claude to add them (under `[data-skin="pop"]`: `tests/pop.test.js` fails the build for any rule that could change the default look) |
| After switching, the heading above what you were reading moved | By design: what's in the middle of the screen stays in place, and Pop mode's headings are bigger | Nothing to fix |
| After switching, the page shows another section | `keepPlace()` in `src/theme.js` didn't find anything to hold on to (a new kind of element?) | Tell Claude, with the section and the screen size (`skintest.mjs` checks 6 places × 3 screen sizes) |

**Tests:** `tests/pop.test.js` (8: the button on both pages, after the theme button, pressed at first, and the menu row; the
ribbons repeat only what the page already says, hidden from screen readers, no money talk; every rule scoped to
`[data-skin="pop"]` except a few shared sizing rules, `!important` only for "reduce motion", nothing from other sites; the
fonts are real WOFF2 files with their licenses and `font-display: swap`; `/theme.js` in a sandbox (Pop mode and dark unless the visitor saved `lab` / `light`,
private mode gets the defaults, the browser-bar color for every page × theme × look matches `src/theme.js`); where the menu
starts in each look; switching keeps your place). End to end, `skintest.mjs` (written before Pop mode became the default, so it expects it off at first; 38: off by default without downloading its fonts; pressed: the look, its
fonts, remembered, the browser bar, the 3D stage's colors, the focus stays; the theme button inside it; after a reload,
there before the first paint; off again, remembered; yesterday's `/theme.js`; the top bar's band; the menu at 920 / 1040 px
and closing when Pop mode goes off at 1000 px; phones at 390, 360 (the menu row) and 320; the diary page; no sideways
scrolling at 7 widths × 2 pages × 2 themes; the chat, the Arena and ClankChecker still work; switching keeps your place (the
same section in the middle of the screen, 6 places × on and off × 1440, 390 and 360 px (there with the menu row); at the very
top it stays at the top; slow fonts: kept at once and again when they arrive; a visitor who scrolls meanwhile isn't pulled
back); "reduce motion"; axe 0 issues on both pages, computer and phone with the menu open, both themes; a clean console).
Every earlier suite passes too (the launch suite's top-bar check now includes the ✦ button).
